stories.headline: Iran says it hit a US base in retaliation as Trump threatens Oman and rejects draft peace deal

key_facts.fact: US forces carried out new 'defensive' strikes on an Iranian naval base and airport in the Strait of Hormuz area late Wednesday, May 27, targeting a military site said to threaten US forces and commercial traffic.
key_facts.excerpt: Donald Trump's military launched more strikes late on Wednesday targeting a military site that was believed to have posed a threat to American forces and commercial traffic in the Strait.

key_facts.fact: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it targeted a US air base in retaliation early Thursday and warned that any further US aggression would draw a 'more decisive' response.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it attacked a base without specifying which one, and warned that any further US aggression would draw a 'more decisive' response.

key_facts.fact: Trump threatened to 'blow up' US ally Oman if it did not agree to his demands over control of the Strait of Hormuz.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump on Wednesday threatened to 'blow up' US ally Oman if it didn't agree to his demands around control of the Strait of Hormuz.

key_facts.fact: The White House dismissed Iran's latest terms and rejected reports of a draft peace deal as a 'complete fabrication'; Trump said Iran was 'negotiating on fumes.'
key_facts.excerpt: Mr. Trump said Iran was 'negotiating on fumes,' before adding, 'Maybe we have to go back and finish it, maybe we don't.'

key_facts.fact: The Israeli military declared all areas south of Lebanon's Zahrani River, roughly 25 miles from the border and including Tyre, as 'combat zones' and ordered residents to evacuate ahead of strikes on Hezbollah.
key_facts.excerpt: The Israeli military on Wednesday declared all areas south of Lebanon's Zahrani River -- an area roughly 25 miles from the border -- as 'combat zones' and told residents to evacuate.

key_facts.fact: An Israeli soldier was killed by a Hezbollah drone near the Lebanon border, bringing the number of Israeli troops killed in the war with the group to 23.
key_facts.excerpt: The Israeli military said on Thursday that a soldier was killed the day before by a Hezbollah drone near the Lebanon border, taking to 23 the number of its troops killed in the war.

stories.headline: FAA grounds SpaceX Starship and orders a mishap probe into the V3 booster failure

key_facts.fact: The FAA determined that SpaceX's May 22 Starship Flight 12 launch resulted in a 'mishap' involving the Super Heavy booster as it flew back after stage separation, and ordered a SpaceX-led investigation it will oversee.
key_facts.excerpt: After a thorough assessment of the operation, the FAA has determined the May 22 SpaceX Starship Flight 12 launch resulted in a mishap. The mishap involved the Super Heavy booster as it flew back to the Gulf of America after stage separation.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX must pause all further Starship test launches until the investigation is completed and the FAA approves the final report and any corrective actions.
key_facts.excerpt: This means SpaceX will have to pause any further Starship test launches until the investigation is completed and the results are submitted to the FAA for approval.

key_facts.fact: The booster separated normally but suffered an apparent engine failure during the return burn, causing it to tumble toward the Gulf and most likely explode on impact; there were no reports of public injury or property damage.
key_facts.excerpt: It immediately experienced an apparent engine failure when it tried to perform the sustained burn... This led to the booster tumbling down toward the Gulf before most likely exploding on impact.

key_facts.fact: The grounding diminishes the chance that another Starship test flight occurs before SpaceX's anticipated IPO in mid-June, with a roadshow set for June 4 and an offering that could raise as much as $80 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Diminishing the chance that another will occur before the company's anticipated IPO in mid-June.

key_facts.fact: Despite the booster failure, the upper-stage Starship released 20 mock satellites and ended with a splashdown in the Indian Ocean as planned.
key_facts.excerpt: The spacecraft continued around the world, releasing 20 mock satellites before ending the mission as planned with a fiery splashdown in the Indian Ocean.

stories.headline: FDA approves AbbVie's Decnupaz for a rare, aggressive blood cancer

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved Decnupaz (pivekimab sunirine-pvzy) on May 27 for adults with blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm (BPDCN), an ultra-rare and aggressive blood cancer with limited treatment options.
key_facts.excerpt: AbbVie today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved DECNUPAZ (pivekimab sunirine-pvzy) for the treatment of adult patients with BPDCN, an ultra-rare and aggressive hematologic malignancy.

key_facts.fact: Approval was supported by the Phase 1/2 CADENZA trial, a multicenter, open-label study in patients with CD123-positive hematologic malignancies including BPDCN.
key_facts.excerpt: The approval is supported by data from the Phase 1/2 CADENZA trial, a global study evaluating the safety and efficacy of DECNUPAZ for BPDCN.

key_facts.fact: In newly diagnosed, treatment-naive patients (n=33), the composite complete response rate was 69.7% with a median duration of response of 9.7 months.
key_facts.excerpt: Newly diagnosed patients with BPDCN (n=33) demonstrated a composite complete response rate of 69.7% with a median duration of response of 9.7 months.

key_facts.fact: Patients with relapsed or refractory disease (n=51) had a composite complete response rate of 15.7%.
key_facts.excerpt: Patients with relapsed or refractory disease (n=51) had a composite complete response rate of 15.7% with median duration of response rate of 9.2 months.

key_facts.fact: Decnupaz is a CD123-directed antibody and alkylating agent conjugate designed to target BPDCN cells.
key_facts.excerpt: Decnupaz is a CD123-directed antibody and alkylating agent conjugate designed to target BPDCN cells.

stories.headline: Bank of Korea holds rate at 2.50% and lifts growth outlook as oil-driven inflation mounts

key_facts.fact: The Bank of Korea held its policy rate steady at 2.50% on Thursday, May 28, the eighth consecutive meeting without a change.
key_facts.excerpt: The Bank of Korea's latest decision marked the eighth consecutive meeting without a change.

key_facts.fact: It was the first rate decision under new Governor Shin Hyun-song, who took office on April 21.
key_facts.excerpt: The first under new Governor Shin Hyun-song, who took office on April 21.

key_facts.fact: The central bank raised its 2026 growth outlook to 2.6%.
key_facts.excerpt: Bank of Korea holds policy rate steady at 2.50%, ups 2026 growth outlook to 2.6%.

key_facts.fact: Consumer prices accelerated 2.6% in April from a year earlier, the fastest gain in 21 months, driven by rising petroleum costs after the US-Iran conflict.
key_facts.excerpt: Consumer prices accelerated 2.6% in April from a year earlier, the fastest gain in 21 months, driven by rising petroleum costs after the US-Iran conflict.

key_facts.fact: South Korea's GDP rose 1.7% quarter-on-quarter in the first quarter, nearly double the central bank's February forecast.
key_facts.excerpt: South Korea's economy rebounded sharply in the first quarter, with GDP rising 1.7% quarter-on-quarter, nearly double the central bank's February forecast.

key_facts.fact: Some economists expect the BOK to raise rates at least twice this year, potentially lifting the benchmark to 3.00%.
key_facts.excerpt: Some economists expect the BOK to raise rates at least twice this year, potentially lifting the benchmark to 3.00%.

stories.headline: GCHQ chief warns of a 'narrowing window' against China and Russia in first annual lecture

key_facts.fact: GCHQ director Anne Keast-Butler delivered the agency's inaugural annual lecture at Bletchley Park on Wednesday, May 27, warning the UK and allies have only a 'narrowing window' to stay ahead of technology threats from Russia and China.
key_facts.excerpt: The UK and its allies have only a 'narrowing window' to stay ahead of technology threats from Russia and China, the head of the UK's spy agency GCHQ will warn today.

key_facts.fact: She accused Russia of 'scaling up its daily hybrid activity' and 'relentlessly targeting critical infrastructure, democratic processes, supply chains and public trust.'
key_facts.excerpt: Russia is 'relentlessly targeting critical infrastructure, democratic processes, supply chains and public trust' and the speed of advancements in technology mean there is a 'narrowing window for the UK and allies to stay ahead.'

key_facts.fact: Keast-Butler called for making cyber security '10 times more urgent' and said everyone 'from board rooms to living rooms' has a role to play in national security.
key_facts.excerpt: It means hardwiring security into new technologies, protecting supply chains and making cyber security '10 times more urgent,' she will say.

key_facts.fact: She said 'China is now a science and tech superpower' with sophisticated capabilities across its intelligence, cyber and military agencies.
key_facts.excerpt: 'China is now a science and tech superpower - with sophisticated capabilities across their intelligence, cyber and military agencies,' she will say.

key_facts.fact: Keast-Butler said GCHQ has, in the past few months, developed the blueprint for a new national cyber defence capability that will 'hardwire cutting-edge agentic AI into machine speed cyber defence.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'GCHQ has developed the blueprint for a new national cyber defence capability that will hardwire cutting-edge agentic AI into machine speed cyber defence.'

sources.title: UK has 'narrowing window' to stay ahead of tech threats, says GCHQ chief Keast-Butler

stories.headline: JD.com founder vows to protect 900,000 workers from being replaced by AI and robots

key_facts.fact: JD.com founder Liu Qiangdong vowed in an internal speech on May 27 to prevent the e-commerce firm's 900,000-strong workforce from losing their jobs to automation.
key_facts.excerpt: Liu Qiangdong has vowed to prevent the e-commerce firm's 900,000-strong workforce from losing their jobs to automation... Mr Liu said in an internal speech on May 27, according to a video circulating on social media.

key_facts.fact: Liu said the company will 'do everything possible to safeguard employment' and that 'JD.com will not fire a single front-line worker replaced by machines.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'JD.com will not fire a single front-line worker replaced by machines,' he said.

key_facts.fact: JD has set up more than 80 training bases ('robobase') around the country to retrain blue-collar workers in skills such as maintenance and servicing of automated systems.
key_facts.excerpt: The online retailer has also set up more than 80 training bases around the country, saying they will serve to retrain workers with skills such as maintenance and servicing of automated systems.

key_facts.fact: The pledge follows a Chinese court ruling in late April that companies cannot terminate employees or cut their salaries just to replace them with AI systems.
key_facts.excerpt: Liu's comments come after a Chinese court ruled in late April that companies cannot terminate employees or cut their salaries just to replace them with artificial intelligence systems.

key_facts.fact: JD already runs a fully automated warehouse, opened in 2018, that handles 200,000 orders a day with just four human employees who service the robots.
key_facts.excerpt: The company opened a fully automated warehouse in 2018 that handles 200,000 orders a day with four human employees, all of whom service the robots.

stories.headline: Record-breaking heat dome bakes western Europe, spiking power prices and straining grids

key_facts.fact: A 'heat dome' of warm air from north Africa pushed temperatures well above May norms across western Europe, with the heat wave forecast to last through the week and intensify further.
key_facts.excerpt: Hit by a so-called 'heat dome' of warm air from northern Africa that is pushing the mercury well above normal levels for May... the heat wave could last through the week.

key_facts.fact: Temperatures in Germany were forecast as high as 30C, with much of France above 30C during midday peaks, for Thursday, May 28.
key_facts.excerpt: Temperatures in Germany are expected to be as high as 30 degrees Celsius on Thursday, and above 30C during midday peaks in much of France.

key_facts.fact: German day-ahead power prices jumped 29% on Wednesday, May 27, as the heat wave raised cooling demand while lower wind generation forced reliance on more expensive gas- and coal-fired plants.
key_facts.excerpt: German day-ahead power prices jumped 29% on Wednesday as a heat wave across much of Europe raised cooling needs, while lower wind generation meant that more expensive electricity production sources, such as gas and coal-fired power plants, would be needed.

key_facts.fact: German wind power output was forecast to fall 9.7 GW day-on-day to 4.4 GW for Thursday delivery, with residual non-renewable load seen rising 8.2 GW to 23.5 GW.
key_facts.excerpt: German wind power output was forecast to fall by 9.7 gigawatts day on day to 4.4 GW for Thursday delivery... residual load was seen rising by 8.2 GW to 23.5 GW.

key_facts.fact: Cooling degree days, a measure of air-conditioning demand, were at their highest level in decades, with the warm pattern expected to persist through the weekend.
key_facts.excerpt: Cooling degree days, a measure of demand for air conditioning, were at their highest level in decades over the period... the warm pattern is expected to persist through the weekend.

key_facts.fact: Scientists say human-driven climate change is amplifying such extremes, making heat waves, droughts and floods more intense and frequent.
key_facts.excerpt: Scientists say human-driven climate change is amplifying such extremes, with weather events like heat waves, droughts and floods becoming more intense and frequent.
